judgments.reasoning_cat1: It acknowledges reading a set of named external documents plus "other material provided by NOLS describing or related to my program," an open catch-all after specifics, and says staff "has been available" rather than that anything was actually explained. The reach of the incorporated material is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether the Catalog, website and Enrollment Packet become terms matters against c024's "MAY BE MODIFIED ONLY IN WRITING" and the assumption of risk in c016, since outside materials could describe risks or standards differently. That is a plausible but unproven fit problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out "except with respect to an injury or other loss which occurs on lands whose rules or regulations prohibit my doing so as a matter of law" is opaque — which lands, whose rules, and what makes a prohibition operate "as a matter of law" are all left open — while "ALL risks... inherent or otherwise" is deliberately sweeping. This is a one-sided drafter's clause with a namable ambiguous exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with c002's inherent-risk definition, with c017's parallel but separately worded carve-out, and with c009/c014's negligence-adjacent disclaimers; assuming "ALL risks" including negligence sits uneasily with c017's express exclusion of gross negligence. A court construing the release would necessarily construe this alongside it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the operative exculpatory and indemnity clause: it releases "any and all claims... arising in whole or part from" participation, includes negligence "but not of gross negligence," is to be "enforced to the fullest extent permitted by law," and carries the same murky lands-rules carve-out. Each of those phrases is a standard battleground, and the clause is drafted wholly in the drafter's favour, so any ambiguity is construed against NOLS.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its defined "Released Parties" omit the contractors disclaimed in c014 and the staff who under c011 act "as private individuals" during free time, and its scope must be squared with c016's assumption of ALL risks and c023's severability. Those interactions give a court more than one place to find inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "No past or current physical or psychological condition that might affect... participation" and "all pertinent medical conditions have been disclosed" set an indefinite standard, and NOLS may remove a student "for any reason it deems in the best interests" — discretion with no measurable boundary. A misrepresentation fight would turn on "might affect" and "pertinent."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The disclaimer that admission is not a representation that staff can manage a medical event sits alongside c019's authorisation for NOLS to provide advanced care under written Medical Protocols, which is close to an assumed standard; the two are in mild tension. No outright contradiction was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Costs reasonably associated with medical services, including evacuation, shall be borne by me" hinges on the undefined qualifier "reasonably," and the reference to care "under the guidance of the NOLS Physician Advisor by way of NOLS' written Medical Protocols" imports an unattached external document. Both are namable but modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Medical Protocols reference arguably creates a standard of care that sits against the release of negligence in c017 and the no-representation sentence in c018. That is a real but secondary tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Environmental organizations or strategic partners in which NOLS graduates may be interested" is vague at the edges, but the grant of permission itself is clear and unconditional. Little turns on where "strategic partners" stops.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in this short instrument limits use of contact information or images; no conflicting provision exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is plainly one-sided — the student bears all damage to NOLS gear while NOLS bears nothing for the student's stored belongings — and "any damage I... may cause" carries no fault standard. That asymmetry invites contra proferentem, though the words themselves are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the general allocation of risk to the student in c016 and c017; no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any mediation or suit shall occur or be filed only in the State of Wyoming" is the classic ambiguity between the geographic State (allowing the federal court sitting there) and the courts of the State, and the parenthetical about "the laws which might apply the laws of another jurisdiction" is a garbled attempt at excluding conflicts rules. Both the forum wording and the choice-of-law parenthetical are readily contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Wyoming law would govern the enforceability of the release in c017 and the assumption of risk in c016, and the mandatory-forum reading interacts with c023's severability; nothing directly contradicts it, so the risk is chiefly textual.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional severability clause; "any part" and "invalid" are standard and the consequence is stated plainly. Nothing in its own words is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with c017's "enforced to the fullest extent permitted by law" and with the lands-rules carve-outs in c016 and c017, which already handle partial invalidity differently, so a court could be asked whether an invalid release is severed or reformed. That overlap is mild rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It recites reading "THIS PAGE AND THE PREVIOUS 3 PAGES," a page count that may not match the executed document, and binds "THEM, THEIR HEIRS, ESTATE, EXECUTORS AND ADMINISTRATORS" without saying whether wrongful-death beneficiaries are included. The heirs language is the sort of phrase a court is asked to stretch or limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parent signature line is blank for an adult student, yet the clause speaks of "THE PARENT(S) OR GUARDIAN OF A MINOR STUDENT," and the writing-only modification rule sits against c015's incorporation of catalogue and website material. Neither is a squarely conflicting operative term.
